strings.name: Mark Schneider
strings.role: Non-executive director of Roche; Siemens Supervisory Board member; former Nestlé CEO
strings.summary: Mark Schneider is a German and US business executive who led Fresenius Group and Nestlé, spanning healthcare and food. After leaving Nestlé, he continued in corporate governance at Roche and Siemens. His career illustrates the distinction between operational leadership and oversight through boards of directors and supervisory boards.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Distinguishes Fresenius Group and Fresenius Medical Care, joining a company and starting as CEO, and Siemens' planned 2027 chair succession and current office.
strings.influence.rationale: Previously led Fresenius and Nestlé, participating in business restructuring in healthcare and global food companies.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a finance and accounting degree at St. Gallen in 1988, a doctorate there in 1992 and a Harvard Business School MBA in 1993.
strings.facts.f2.label: Current offices and plans
strings.facts.f2.value: Serves as a Roche non-executive director and Siemens Supervisory Board member; Siemens plans to elect him chair after its 2027 AGM, an appointment not yet effective.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Management across industries
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from Haniel into healthcare, first as Fresenius Medical Care CFO, then Fresenius Group CEO, before leading Nestlé.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From management to oversight
strings.highlights.h2.text: His Nestlé CEO and director roles ended effective September 1, 2024; his Roche directorship and Siemens supervisory role belong to separate companies' governance structures.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Named in Siemens chair succession plan
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Supervisory Board announced its intention to elect him chair after the February 11, 2027 AGM; this was a future plan.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Attends Roche AGM and is re-elected
strings.timeline.t2.text: The minutes confirm his attendance; shareholders re-elected him to the board for one year.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Elected to Siemens Supervisory Board
strings.timeline.t3.text: Shareholders elected him to the supervisory body, distinct from the Managing Board or CEO role.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Ends Nestlé service
strings.timeline.t4.text: His resignation as CEO and director became effective, with Laurent Freixe succeeding him as CEO.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joins Roche board
strings.timeline.t5.text: The official company biography dates his board membership from 2023.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Nestlé CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined the company for an introductory period in September 2016 and formally took over as CEO the following January.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes Fresenius Group CEO
strings.timeline.t7.text: Moved from a finance role at Fresenius Medical Care into the group's top executive role, serving until 2016.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Becomes Fresenius Medical Care CFO
strings.timeline.t8.text: Moved from Haniel to Fresenius Medical Care to oversee finance.
